palette.notes: Not digital pixel art: a physical fuse-bead (Perler) Miku figure. Measured palette_size 49 (one ramp, hue shift 30) reflects the photo, light and table. By eye: flat skin, brown and white tones with black outline beads.

lighting: Real room light on a physical object; the bead art carries its own flat cel shading (a darker skin tone on the legs, grey under the dress).
silhouette: Every bead edge is outlined in black beads, so the figure reads clearly against the blue gingham cloth even when cropped.

motion.timing: Measured 29.89 drawings/s, median hold 33.3 ms (on 1s): this is live camera motion, not animation. Close-up tweezer placement for ~3.5 s, then a pull-back pan along the finished figure.

texture: Round bead holes give a dotted, tactile grid; the tweezers placing a single bead show the scale.
camera: Handheld phone: starts macro on the shoe with tweezers, then pans and pulls back up the legs to the face for the reveal at ~6-8 s.

acting.acts: No acting; the character is a static craft piece. The staging teaches the reveal: show one tiny part being made, then travel to the whole.
acting.depth: Macro close-up first, full figure last; scale contrast is the hook.

techniques: not pixel art in the digital sense: a fuse-bead build, noted here for staging only
camera travel along the figure as the reveal (feet to face)
black outline beads keep the figure readable on a busy patterned background
POV caption on screen for the first ~5 s
feel: tiny tweezer detail + slow pan to the face = satisfying craft reveal (not digital pixel art)
for_fred: Use the detail-to-whole reveal: open on an extreme close-up of one part of Fred (a fin, an eye), then pull back to show all of him; keep a dark outline so he reads on a busy background.
